paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. This body is a tent, and tents come down. Paul says if this earthly tent is dismantled, "we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands" (2 Corinthians 5:1). So the groaning isn't the end of the story, because something better is coming.

And you're not waiting with empty hands. Paul says it is God who "has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come" (2 Corinthians 5:5). Right now we walk "by faith, not by sight" (2 Corinthians 5:7). That's why Paul can be confident even while we're away from the Lord, and I'm telling you, friend, that kind of confidence beats a full tray of cookies.

So what do we do while the tent is still up? Paul says "we aspire to please Him, whether we are at home in this body or away from it" (2 Corinthians 5:9). He gives the reason right after: "we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ" (2 Corinthians 5:10). Live today like the ovens are warm and the Lord is worth pleasing.
